newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods mixed with margins soft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods mixed with margins soft.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined products markets were narrowly mixed in razor-thin trade Thursday as supply remained ample and refiners looked at scaling back crude use, traders said.
"It's extremely quiet out there," one trader said.

Refiners appeared to avoid the market Thursday, as profits remained thin. In the quarter so far, margins stand at $6.35 a barrel, compared $9.05 at the same time last year, according to analyst reports.
Tosco Corp already cut crude oil runs early last week and Chevron is rumored to be trimming crude input as well.
Although U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTi) crude is down from last quarter, at $20.17 versus $23 in the first three month of 1997, products also remain low, traders said.

Gasoline stocks meanwhile fell by a neutral 166,000 barrels to 29.4 million barrels and distillate stocks fell by 224,000 barrels to 11.7 million barrels, according to trade group American Petroleum Institute.
Regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline was pegged between 62.50 and 63.50 cents a gallon in San Francisco, with Los Angeles 0.25 cents stronger. Both cities saw prices up 0.75 to 1.00 cents.
Regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was pegged at between 59 and 61 cents a gallon, steady with Wednesday, with most refineries operating normally.
Distillate prices in Los Angeles were steady to higher, with CARB-grade low sulphur, low aromatic diesel pegged 0.50 cents a gallon higher in LA between 64.50/65.50 cents a gallon.
